faa_runway_anchor_to_aldot_runway_polygo.reference: FAA Runway 36-end anchor reused by the taxi-hold node

interpretation.crs_or_origin_diagnosis: The near-zero Taxiway A alignment and runway anchors near FAA/ALDOT pavement argue against a single large translation or axis-sign error. The major production discrepancies are localized to approximate apron access, assumed stand locations, and service connectors. This is a consistency diagnosis, not a survey-accuracy claim.

method.coordinate_system: WGS 84 geographic (EPSG:4326) source polygons transformed to FAA KAUO ENU meters (EPSG:4979 origin); graph and polygons audited without post-hoc alignment
method.distance: minimum Euclidean point-to-polygon distance in airport-local ENU meters; inside a valid polygon is 0 m
method.edge_sampling: 101 evenly spaced samples including each endpoint per straight graph edge
method.known_transform_limitation: ALDOT service query supplied 4326 geometry; original 3857 geometry was not separately acquired for an independent projection round-trip check

origin.source: FAA 28 Day NASR APT_BASE, effective 2026-10-01; ARPT_PSN_SOURCE=3RD PARTY SURVEY, POSITION_SRC_DATE=2006/05/22. Ellipsoid height is the published field elevation converted to meters plus approximate GEOID18 separation (-28.56 m).

method.surfaces: ALDOT outer boundaries and interior rings; aircraft-operable RUNWAY, TAXIWAY, and APRON classifications only
